children: shares rose 3.90% premarket after announcing a partnership with Anthropic to build a team of embedded evaluators inside Anthropic to red-team its models, run alignment assessments, and test safeguards. Both companies said they expect to invest at least $1 billion each over the next five years on the effort.

The work will be led by Faculty, the applied AI safety firm Accenture acquired, which has evaluated models for other AI labs and helped build systems including the UK National Health Service's COVID-era Early Warning System. Accenture chair and CEO Julie Sweet framed embedded evaluation as an emerging discipline the company wants to help scale, while Faculty CEO Marc Warner said the work reflects a belief that AI should be "safe by design, not safe by accident."

Anthropic tied the move to CEO Dario Amodei's essay calling on the industry to pace frontier development, describing embedded evaluators as having access "comparable to an employee's," able to watch models take shape in training and verify the company is keeping its safety commitments. Anthropic said the arrangement isn't exclusive, and that it plans to add more evaluator partnerships in the coming weeks.

title: Accenture Stock Rises 4% on $1 Billion Anthropic Safety Deal
